recommendation: Keep this source fix as-is. It closes the remaining current-source ConceptMap2 reference found during reconciliation without reopening the already-applied ConceptMap redesign. Related precursor or later cleanup tickets should remain separately audited if needed.
issue_request: FHIR-32855 was a Published/Persuasive Vocabulary WG FHIR-core ConceptMap issue for R5. It requested that the temporary ConceptMap2 resource replace ConceptMap and then be removed from the specification, including the resource list.
initial_application: No explicitly Jira-tagged source commit for FHIR-32855 was found. Commit 8623473ddfcef0cb88b9abf5241abfe6e28ea542 effectively applied the main transition by moving ConceptMap2 source files and definitions into the active ConceptMap resource and removing the conceptmap2 resource entry from source/fhir.ini. The ConceptMap2 entry in implementations/translations.xml had been added earlier and was not touched by that replacement commit.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini actively lists conceptmap=ConceptMap and no conceptmap2 resource entry, and the source/conceptmap2 folder is absent. publish.ini still publishes implementations/translations.xml as translations.xml, and source/downloads.html links it as translations of common FHIR names and messages, making the stale ConceptMap2 translation entry part of the current published implementation artifact surface. Confluence and Zulip evidence from July/August 2022 confirms the work group considered ConceptMap2 replaced/discarded as a separate resource.
reconciliation: Removed the orphaned ConceptMap2 item from implementations/translations.xml. No other ConceptMap source change was needed because the active ConceptMap StructureDefinition and resource list already reflect the replacement.
source_changes: implementations/translations.xml: removed the stale item id="ConceptMap2" and its language translations.

related_jiras.note: Created the temporary ConceptMap2 StructureDefinition and resource-list entry that FHIR-32855 later replaced and discarded.
